results.title: Who Is Authorized to Perform GMP Sampling? QA, QC, or Production Operators?
results.content: # Who May Perform Sampling in GMP? Sampling of raw materials, intermediates, bulk and finished products is a **quality-critical GMP activity**. * **QA/QC personnel** have the primary responsibility and oversight for sampling. * **Production personnel may perform sampling** if:. For high-risk materials (sterile APIs, highly toxic substances, controlled materials, or regulatory witness sampling), only **QA/QC or specialized teams** should perform sampling. Conditions for Allowing Production Personnel to Sample. * Specific training in sampling techniques, container handling, contamination control, and documentation. * SOPs must define when and how production staff may sample, what materials are covered, and under what supervisory framework. * QA/QC retains approval and oversight, even if production personnel execute sampling. Chain-of-Custody & Sample Integrity. When Production Staff Should NOT Sample. **Q: Does production staff sampling violate GMP?**. 1. Document all sampling requirements in SOPs. 2. Ensure training and qualification of all sampling personnel. 4. Restrict high-risk sampling to QA/QC or specialized personnel.

results.content: # Site Replication. Site replication configures multiple independent AIStor deployments as a cluster of replicas called peer sites. Site replication supports the included AIStor IDP, OIDC, or LDAP. Configuring replication between sites with mismatched AIStor versions may result in unexpected or undesired replication behavior. ### What replicates across all sites. ### What does not replicate across sites. AIStor deployments in a site replication configuration do *not* replicate the creation or modification of the following items:. AIStor by default replicates the key ID used to encrypt an object on the source site to all peers. The peer sites use their own encryption configurations to encrypt the replicated object. Any AIStor deployment in the site replication configuration can resynchronize damaged replica-eligible data from the peer with the most updated (“latest”) version of that data. `--purge-on-delete` on individual buckets in a deployment with site replication enabled is supported on AIStor `RELEASE.2025-03-31T22-43-59Z` or later.

results.title: What is Data Replication Storage | Hevo
results.content: # What is Data Replication Storage: An In-depth Guide. In this article, we are going to take a look at data replication and replication storage. Once done reading, you’ll have an in-depth knowledge of the data replication storage strategy, its implementation, advantages, and disadvantages, etc. ## What is Data Replication? With data replication, organizations can disseminate data across various storage locations, including different regions, on-site and off-site hosts, and cloud servers. ## Benefits of Data Replication. Some of the benefits of data replication are as follows:. * **Enhanced Server Performance:** Data replication helps reduce the load on the primary server by distributing data across numerous storage regions/locations, thereby boosting the network performance. ## How Does Data Replication Work? Data replication involves one or more applications that are capable of connecting a primary storage location with a secondary location. There are several ways to replicate data. Data replication based on the timing of data transfer is classified as follows:. Replication Storage, also known as storage-based replication, is an approach to replicating data available over a network to numerous distinct storage locations/regions. Storage-based data replication makes use of software installed on the storage device to handle the replication. In storage system-based local replication, the data replication is carried out within the storage system. In simple words, one of the storage systems is on the source site and the other storage system is on a remote site for data replication. Storage-Based Replication and Host-Based Replication are the two most widely used Data Replication techniques. On the other hand, as discussed in the previous section, the storage-based replication process requires setting up and implementing a **SAN** to replicate data. It leverages numerous software and applications to replicate data from the primary data storage in real-time. This software further allows users to achieve real-time replication across the storage layer, thereby helping them unleash the power of data replication. Various vendors support implementing storage-based replication to create multiple copies across numerous regions and ensure high data availability. * Understanding the Need of Data Replication Strategy. This article teaches you in-depth & answers all your queries about Replication Storage or storage-based data replication strategy.
